headline: Regulators brand frontier AI the financial system's gravest cyber risk as attackers weaponize and impersonate it, while nearly 22,000 Exchange servers stay open to mailbox hijacking.

emerging_trends.text: Andrew Bailey's Financial Stability Board branded frontier AI finance's most immediate cyber risk days after Forescout drove Claude to port a live PLC exploit in hours for a few hundred dollars.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Frontier AI Sharpens Attacks and Systemic Risk

emerging_trends.text: Iran's Nimbus Manticore now hides its NodeRabbit and PollCat RATs inside recruiter coding tests to reach Linux and macOS, a cross-platform pivot that widens its espionage beyond Windows.
Criminals keep trading on AI hype, packing RevStealer into a bogus 'Claude Opus 5' download and relabeling rogue inference servers with premium model names to trap coding agents.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Malware Poses as Free AI Tools

topics.title: Nimbus Manticore Builds Cross-Platform RATs
topics.latest_developments: The Hacker News reported Iran's Nimbus Manticore now poses as recruiters handing developers coding tests that drop the Node.js RAT NodeRabbit and the JavaScript RAT PollCat, extending the group onto Linux and macOS, with Kaspersky first spotting NodeRabbit in Afghanistan before variants surfaced in Egypt and Ethiopia.
topics.summary: Nimbus Manticore, an IRGC-linked espionage crew Kaspersky also calls Mirage Kitten, targets aviation and financial-technology developers; teams should treat unsolicited recruiter coding assignments as a malware-delivery vector.

sources.title: Iranian Hackers Pose as Recruiters to Deliver Cross-Platform RATs Through Coding Tests
Iranian cyber spies target aviation, fintech developers with new malware
Mirage Kitten targeting aviation and FinTech sectors across the Middle East and Africa with a new malware set

topics.title: Frontier AI Sharpens Attacks and Systemic Risk
topics.latest_developments: Financial Stability Board chair Andrew Bailey called cyber risk from frontier AI the 'most immediate concern' to the global financial system and told firms to prepare for simultaneous disruption across shared technology dependencies, while Forescout researchers used Claude AI to port a WAGO PLC remote-code-execution exploit between models in hours for a few hundred dollars.
topics.summary: Regulators and researchers warn that capable AI models compress the time and cost of building working exploits and concentrate systemic risk; institutions should assume attackers now wield the same tools.

sources.title: Cyber risk from frontier AI poses 'most immediate concern' to global financial system, watchdog warns
Experiment: Porting a PLC Exploit With AI Takes Hours and Hundreds of Dollars

topics.title: Malware Poses as Free AI Tools
topics.latest_developments: Morphisec found a GitHub repository impersonating Anthropic and offering free 'Claude Opus 5' access that instead drops RevStealer, a quiet Windows infostealer that hunts passwords and cryptocurrency-wallet data, while a SANS honeypot caught operators relabeling an exposed inference endpoint with sought-after model names to lure a real coding-agent session and harvest its files and tool manifest.
topics.summary: Attackers exploit demand for premium AI models by disguising malware and rogue 'free' LLM backends; users should pull AI clients only from official vendor channels and distrust free model endpoints.

sources.title: Fake Claude Opus 5 app delivers malware and wipes its own tracks
The Coding-Agent Trap: When a "Free" LLM Endpoint Is the Adversary

topics.title: Thousands of Exchange Servers Await Patch
topics.latest_developments: BleepingComputer counted nearly 22,000 internet-exposed Microsoft Exchange servers still unpatched against a high-severity authentication-bypass flaw that lets attackers hijack every mailbox on a host.
topics.summary: The flaw hits on-premises Microsoft Exchange deployments; administrators should apply Microsoft's fix at once to block full mailbox takeover.

sources.title: Nearly 22,000 Microsoft Exchange servers vulnerable to hijack attacks

topics.title: GOLD SHERWOOD Ransomware Tradecraft Exposed
topics.latest_developments: Sophos published an analysis of 15 intrusions that maps the tradecraft of affiliates behind the GOLD SHERWOOD ransomware operation.
topics.summary: GOLD SHERWOOD is an affiliate-driven ransomware operation; defenders can turn the documented tactics into detections and hunting rules.

sources.title: Ungentlemanly behavior: Insights into a ransomware operation

business_politics.title: Tankers Attacked in Strait of Hormuz
business_politics.latest_developments: Attackers hit two tankers carrying Saudi and South Korean crude on a midnight run through the Strait of Hormuz, and President Trump summoned U.S. refiners to the White House for a Tuesday meeting on fuel prices.
business_politics.summary: Renewed U.S.-Iran fighting pushed crude higher on September 1 as strikes hit vessels laden with Saudi and South Korean oil in the Strait of Hormuz, the chokepoint that carries much of the world's seaborne supply; Iran's president said Tehran would return to the ceasefire if Washington does.

business_politics.title: Global Bond Rout Deepens as Inflation Fears Build
business_politics.latest_developments: Eurozone inflation climbed to 3.3% in August, setting up a European Central Bank rate increase next week, as U.K. borrowing costs hit their highest since 2008 and rate-hike expectations spread to the Federal Reserve.
business_politics.summary: Government bonds sold off worldwide on September 1 as rising oil prices revived inflation fears, driving yields higher across the United Kingdom, Japan, and the United States and lifting the odds that major central banks raise rates; gold held below $4,500 an ounce as the selloff sapped its appeal.

business.title: Burgettstown Data Center Splits Washington County
business.latest_developments: More than 100 residents packed a Washington County fire hall to clash over a Burgettstown-area data center proposal, and officials scheduled four more public hearings.
business.summary: A large data center project near Burgettstown has divided Washington County residents, some charging that leaders "sold off the whole community," as the plan advances toward four additional public hearings.

sources.title: More than 100 pack Washington County fire hall as residents clash over data center project

business.title: AI Horizons Summit Comes to Pittsburgh
business.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette previewed an AI Horizons summit built to confront the friction around artificial intelligence, drawing figures from Waymo and Governor Josh Shapiro.
business.summary: Organizers of the AI Horizons summit plan to gather technologists from the self-driving firm Waymo, the startup Gecko, and Governor Josh Shapiro in Pittsburgh to work through the uncomfortable tensions artificial intelligence creates.

sources.title: 'It's all about the tension': Upcoming artificial intelligence summit to explore uncomfortable issues

around_town.title: Washington County Water Main Break
around_town.latest_developments: A 24-inch water main broke in Washington County, cutting service to nearly 100 customers, with repairs expected to run up to 23 hours.
around_town.summary: A 24-inch water main break forced crews to shut off service across parts of Washington County on September 1, leaving nearly 100 customers with no water, low pressure, or cloudy water while emergency repairs proceeded.

around_town.summary: Western Pennsylvania faces heat indexes near the mid-90s followed by severe storms carrying damaging winds, large hail, and a tornado risk on Wednesday and Thursday, September 2 and 3, with scattered storm chances lingering into Friday.

events.title: Oktoberfest Returns as 'PROSTBURGH'
events.latest_developments: The Pittsburgh Downtown Partnership and Flyspace Productions announced Oktoberfest Pittsburgh will run October 1 through 11, rebranding Downtown as "PROSTBURGH."
events.summary: Oktoberfest Pittsburgh runs Thursday, October 1, through Sunday, October 11, across Downtown's Golden Triangle, with German-inspired food, beer, music, games, and family activities staged by the Pittsburgh Downtown Partnership and Flyspace Productions.

events.title: Golden Hour Pop-Up Before Kacey Musgraves
events.latest_developments: The Pittsburgh Parks Conservancy and First National Bank will host a free "Golden Hour" Parkside Pop-Up ahead of Kacey Musgraves's concert.
events.summary: A free "Golden Hour" Parkside Pop-Up runs Tuesday, September 8, at Frankie Pace Park, hosted by the Pittsburgh Parks Conservancy and First National Bank, ahead of Kacey Musgraves's concert that night at PPG Paints Arena.

around_teams.title: Pirates Open Final Month at PNC Park
around_teams.latest_developments: TribLive and the Post-Gazette framed the Pirates' September, watching whether ace Paul Skenes gains traction and eyeing call-up candidates Rafael Flores and Braxton Ashcraft.
around_teams.summary: The Pirates return to PNC Park on Tuesday, September 1, for their first home game since winning road series over the St. Louis Cardinals and San Diego Padres, entering the season's final month with postseason hopes dwindling as beat writers track Paul Skenes and September promotions.

team_usa.title: Plum Out for Season, Misses FIBA World Cup
team_usa.latest_developments: The Phoenix Mercury said Kelsey Plum will miss the rest of the 2026 WNBA season, and she will also sit out the FIBA Women's World Cup alongside A'ja Wilson.
team_usa.summary: USA Basketball will play the FIBA Women's World Cup without Kelsey Plum and A'ja Wilson, both sidelined for health reasons, with Kiki Iriafen and Sonia Citron taking their roster spots.
